newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen staging strong rally on Dow record.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen staging strong rally on Dow record.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to continue their strong rally on Tuesday after the Dow industrials surged to a record high on Monday, brokers said.
"It's going to go up a lot. In terms of index, I am sure we would see a decent 200 points on the index by the end of the day," said Adrian Faure, research director at Merrill Lynch.
The Dow industrials jumped 143.29 points, or 2.03 percent, to an all-time closing high of 7,214.49 on Monday, buoyed by hopes that inflation remained in check.
The Hang Seng Index surged 317.64 points, or 2.43 percent, to finish at 13,399.34 on Monday.
"The Dow's up two percent, bond yields are continuing to come down, inflation rate fears are receding and these are the drivers of Hong Kong today," Faure said.
Blue chips should continue to dominate trading and overseas money was seen returning to the Hong Kong market, said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

The blue-chip index has risen 789.92 points or 6.34 percent in the past four trading days. Brokers said the bull run was likely to continue, with the Hang Seng seen testing its all-time record of 14,004.93 later this week.
